Article Title: 'I resign as CM': CJP's Abhijeet Dipke mocks MP govt after Balaghat heckling
Article Text:
The "announcement" came after Dipke was allegedly heckled by a group of people during his visit to Balaghat

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday mocked the Mohan Yadav-led Madhya Pradesh government and announced his resignation as the state's chief minister.The sarcastic announcement came after Dipke was allegedly heckled by a group of people during his visit to Balaghat district, where more than 30 tribal children have reportedly died from infectious diseases.In a post on X, Dipke wrote: "I hereby resign as the chief minister of MP with immediate effect. I thank Hon’ble PM @narendramodi ji for giving me the opportunity to serve the people of MP, an opportunity in which I have clearly failed."Dipke also shared a purported resignation letter addressed to the Madhya Pradesh governor, in which he took responsibility for the deaths of the tribal children and criticised the state government's response to the tragedy."My conscience does not allow me to continue occupying this chair after the deaths of more than 30 Tribal children in Balaghat. As Chief Minister, I accept responsibility for failing to provide them with the timely medical care and support they needed," the letter said.Dipke further questioned the compensation announced for the victims and alleged that the government had initially offered a lower amount before increasing it following protests by the tribal community."Our response reflects how little value we have placed on the lives of Tribal children," the letter said, while also questioning why health officials had not been held accountable.The CJP founder's post came after his visit to Adori, Korka and Bondari villages in Balaghat, where he met families of tribal children who allegedly died from infectious diseases and gathered information about healthcare facilities.During the visit, a viral video showed a woman, described as a social media influencer, approaching Dipke with a microphone as he was leaving in a car. She questioned whether he had come to "do politics on corpses" and why he had visited the area so late.Dipke was heard apologising for the delayed visit. The woman was also heard saying, "A good road has been constructed here. Can't you see it?"As the confrontation escalated, CJP workers accompanying Dipke moved him into another car and took him away. The woman was then heard saying, "he ran away, he ran away."
Article Summary: The sarcastic announcement came after Dipke was allegedly heckled by a group of people during his visit to Balaghat district. Dipke also shared a purported resignation letter addressed to the Madhya Pradesh governor, in which he took responsibility for the deaths of the tribal children.

Article Title: Xi Jinping arrives in Delhi for Brics summit, set for talks with PM Modi
Article Text:
Xi was received at the Delhi airport by Union Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Jitin Prasada

PM Modi-Xi talks amid efforts to repair ties

Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in New Delhi on Saturday for the 18th BRICS Summit , beginning a two-day visit to India that marks his first trip to the country in seven years.Xi was received at the Delhi airport by Union minister of state for commerce and industry Jitin Prasada, with cultural artistes from the Northeast and other parts of India performing traditional dances to welcome the Chinese leader. The ministry of external affairs said on X, “Warm welcome to President Xi Jinping of the People’s Republic of China on his arrival in New Delhi to attend the 18th BRICS Summit. He was received by MoS @JitinPrasada at the airport. We look forward to constructive discussions as BRICS continues to advance cooperation and contribute to a more balanced, representative and multipolar world.”Xi's arrival comes ahead of his bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, scheduled for 6pm on Saturday.The visit follows a series of high-level engagements between India and China aimed at rebuilding ties after the deadly Galwan Valley clashes in 2020 and the subsequent military standoff in eastern Ladakh.National Security Adviser Ajit Doval held Special Representative talks with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Beijing last month. The discussions covered the India-China boundary question, including delimitation of the frontier, trans-boundary cooperation and maintaining peace along the LAC.Both Doval and Wang are designated Special Representatives for the boundary talks mechanism, established in 2003 to address the 3,488-km India-China border dispute. PM Modi and Xi had also held wide-ranging talks on August 31 last year on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Tianjin.Xi's delegation includes Cai Qi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and director of the General Office of the CPC Central Committee, as well as Wang Yi, a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Chinese foreign minister.
Article Summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in New Delhi on Saturday for the 18th BRICS Summit. Xi's arrival comes ahead of his bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, scheduled for 6pm on Saturday. Visit follows a series of high- level engagements between India and China aimed at rebuilding ties after the deadly Galwan Valley clashes in 2020 and the subsequent military standoff in eastern Ladakh.

Article Title: 'Prioritise national interest': Shashi Tharoor advises govt to keep Brics 'non-West'
Article Text:
Shashi Tharoor says govt must keep Brics non-West and not let it appear anti-West.

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Shashi Tharoor on Friday cautioned that the Brics summit hosted by India should not appear to be an anti-West platform, as that would not be in sync with the country’s national interests.Tharoor, who served as a diplomat at the United Nations for decades, advised the government to showcase the concerns of the Global South while keeping India’s direct national interests in mind."As chair, we have a particular responsibility to showcase both the Brics as a forum, the concerns of the Global South in general, but also while bearing very, very carefully in mind our direct national interests. We want Brics to be a forum that is non-West, but not anti-West. That is exactly actually the same agenda as every other country. There are some others in Brics who are very happy to take it as a geopolitical non-Western, but also anti-Western platform," Tharoor told news agency PTI.He also said that PM Modi's scheduled meeting with Chinese president Xi Jinping and the meeting with Russian president Vladimir Putin "are going to grab world headlines"."And I would like to say that that would not be in India's national interest...Becauseall these world leaders are in India, there will be significant bilateral conversations. Our Prime Minister is bound to be meeting each of the visiting heads of state and government who seeks a meeting. And that may mean a dozen important meetings with these country leaders. And for us, of course, both the meeting with President Xi and the meeting with President Putin are going to grab world headlines," the Thiruvananthapuram Lok Sabha MP said.Former Union minister Salman Khurshid also described the gathering as a “significant event” that allows India to demonstrate leadership on the global stage.Speaking to ANI, Khurshid stressed that the presence of leaders from all 11 member countries, including China, Iran, Russia, South Africa and India, could help New Delhi bring countries together, reduce contradictions and conflicts, and work towards creating better conditions in the world."This is a significant event. We hosted the G20 summit a few years ago, and the important thing is that the top leadership of China, Iran, Russia, South Africa, and India will all be present. All 11 countries will be present. It allows India to demonstrate leadership and ensure that contradictions and conflicts are reduced to a minimum. It can't be done overnight, but at least some attempt should be made. For India to have a locus as the leader and chairperson of the Brics summit, to be able to bring people together, converge, and accept positions that will create better conditions in the world," he said.Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday said leaders from across the world would gather in New Delhi over the next few days for the Brics summit, expressing confidence that the high-level meeting would see positive and meaningful discussions on various issues with the welfare of the world in mind.“Over the next few days, leaders from around the world will gather for the Brics Summit. I am confident that the Summit will see positive and meaningful discussions on various issues with the welfare of the world in mind,” Modi said in a post on X in Hindi.The Prime Minister also shared a Sanskrit shlok highlighting the importance of cultivating relationships with virtuous people and promoting dialogue and goodwill.“A person should always live among the virtuous and cultivate their company. A person should engage in discussion and foster friendly relations with the virtuous, because mutual goodwill, dialogue and friendly relations strengthen peace and cooperation,” the verse said in a loose translation.As Brics chair in 2026, India will host the 18th Brics summit in New Delhi on September 12 and 13. The summit will bring together leaders of Brics member and partner countries, as well as outreach invitees.During the summit, leaders are expected to discuss ways to strengthen intra-Brics cooperation on common priorities and exchange views on global and regional issues of mutual importance, according to a statement issued by the Ministry of External Affairs.Earlier on Thursday night, Bharat Mandapam, the venue for the summit in New Delhi, was being readied to host the high-profile gathering, with leaders and representatives from across the world expected to arrive for the September 12-13 event.
Article Summary: Shashi Tharoor says govt must keep Brics non-West and not let it appear anti- West. PM Modi's scheduled meeting with Chinese president Xi Jinping and the meeting with Russian president Vladimir Putin "are going to grab world headlines"

Article Title: Brics hammers out joint declaration after India bridges Iran-UAE chasm
Article Text:
PM Modi and other Brics lead​ers at the 2026 summit in Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi

NEW DELHI: In a dramatic repeat of the 2023 G20 Declaration under India’s presidency, Brics member-states reached a consensus for a joint declaration following intensive, late-night negotiations that lasted till 4 am on Saturday. The talks had been strained by sharp differences between the UAE and Iran over the West Asia conflict and an earlier meeting of the Brics foreign ministers under India’s presidency had ended without a consensual statement.The 140-paragraph New Delhi Declaration announced by PM Narendra Modi was solidified by a rare leader-level Iran-UAE meeting - between Iran President Masour Pezeshkian and Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan – in the middle of the war that started on February 28.In a delicately worded compromise, the declaration addressed the interests of both sides by expressing serious concerns over deliberate attacks on civilian infrastructure and also peaceful nuclear facilities under full safeguards of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), in violation of international law and relevant resolutions of the IAEA. This implicit criticism of US-Israeli action against Iran was crucial in getting Iran to sign off on the declaration.“We in Brics must fight against the normalization of attacks on civilian, vital infrastructure. The same applies to peaceful nuclear infrastructure," said Pezeshkian at the summit​​​.Nuclear safeguards, safety, and security must always be upheld, including in armed conflicts, to protect people and the environment from harm, said the declaration.Significantly, the joint statement did not name any country or explicitly condemn attacks, prioritising instead dialogue and diplomacy, UN Charter, civilian lives and infrastructure and respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity of all States, while also expressing deep concern over continued escalations and calling for maximum restraint.In the declaration, the leaders recalled their respective national positions on West Asia and stressed the need to work together to maintain smooth flow of global trade, supply chains and energy, in accordance with applicable international law.Official sources said India led prolonged negotiations at multiple levels to reconcile sharp differences between the 2 sides and forge consensus with support from other member-states who were keen that the summit didn’t end without a joint statement.The Brics consensus is reminiscent of the last-minute G20 2023 Delhi declaration that was achieved in the middle of the escalating Russia-Ukraine war with a carefully nuanced formulation that called upon all States to refrain from use of force for territorial acquisition but without naming Russia.The Brics declaration also came days before Iran’s meeting with GCC countries on the Strait of Hormuz situation. In Pezeshkian’s meeting with the crown prince, the leaders underscored the importance of supporting efforts to ease tensions, promote de-escalation and strengthen regional stability.Indian officials had on Friday expressed confidence about a constructive outcome from the negotiations, following Modi’s meeting with Pezeshkian in which he expressed solidarity with Tehran, seeking a long-term and win-win partnership with Iran.On other issues, like in Rio last year, China and Russia, as permanent members of the UN Security Council, reiterated their support to the aspirations of Brazil and India to play a greater role in the UN, including the Security Council.Importantly for India, the declaration expressed strong condemnation of any acts of terrorism as “criminal and unjustifiable, regardless of their motivation, whenever, wherever and by whomsoever committed” and strongly reiterated condemnation of the Pahalgam terrorist attack.“We reaffirm our commitment to combating terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, including the cross-border movement of terrorists, terrorism financing and safe havens,” said the declaration.On the Palestine issue, Brics countries, including India, expressed deep concern on the continued violence in Gaza despite the ceasefire agreement of October 2025. “We call for halting any policies aimed at forced displacement of Palestinians from Gaza Strip and express concern regarding arrangements that may prejudice the inalienable rights of the Palestinian people and legitimize or prolong occupation,” said the declaration.There was no mention of the Ukraine war in the declaration this year. The declaration backed comprehensive reform of the UN, including the Security Council, with a view to making it more “democratic, representative, effective and efficient” and to increase the representation of developing countries in the Council's memberships.
Article Summary: The 140-paragraph New Delhi Declaration announced by PM Narendra Modi was solidified by a rare leader-level Iran-UAE meeting. The talks had been strained by sharp differences between the UAE and Iran over the West Asia conflict. The declaration addressed the interests of both sides by expressing serious concerns over deliberate attacks on civilian infrastructure and peaceful nuclear facilities.

Article Title: Rajnath: Modi blunted oppn's 'false narrative' with governance
Article Text:
Defence minister Rajnath Singh

New Delhi: PM Modi has blended good governance with participatory democracy to render the opposition's "false narrative" and anti-incumbency factor irrelevant, defence minister Rajnath Singh said Saturday, virtually kick-starting BJP's campaign to mark its pre-eminent leader's 25-year unbroken run as head of govt."Those building false narrative against Modi cannot understand what they should do. Sometimes they incite students, sometimes they try to divide society in the name of caste," he said in an apparent swipe at leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi.He said that when people see their lives changed by welfare schemes for farmers, housing and health, then no narrative works. "Kaam bolta hai (work speaks). Modi has left factors like astroturfing and anti-incumbency behind," he said at the event organised by Rambhau Mhalgi Prabodhini, a research and leadership-training institute with links to BJP.Rajnath said Modi, since his days as Gujarat CM, pioneered a model of governance that focused on a participatory model of democracy and scaled it nationally as PM.
Article Summary: Defence minister Rajnath Singh says PM Modi has blended good governance with participatory democracy to render the opposition's "false narrative" irrelevant. He said that when people see their lives changed by welfare schemes for farmers, housing and health, then no narrative works. Modi has left factors like astroturfing and anti-incumbency behind.

Panaji, Hoardings featuring the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and Goa Forward Party (GFP) surfaced along Goa's highways on Saturday, sparking buzz of a new front emerging in the coastal state ahead of AAP convenor Arvind Kejriwal's visit.However, the Congress said alliance talks with the Vijai Sardesai-led GFP were underway for the 2027 assembly polls.Displaying the slogan, "Don't let them cheat you the third time", the hoardings with symbols of AAP and GFP signal an imminent pre-poll arrangement between Kejriwal's party and the Vijai Sardesai's outfit for the 2027 state elections."Am going to Goa today to make a very big announcement," Kejriwal wrote on his X handle on Saturday morning, even as AAP functionaries confirmed he would arrive in the state later during the day.The GFP is a regional outfit led by former deputy chief minister Sardesai, who is the party's lone MLA in the state assembly, while the AAP has two MLAs - Venzy Viegas and Cruz Silva - representing Benaulim and Velim constituencies respectively in South Goa.A senior GFP functionary said Kejriwal will address a press conference on Sunday during which the alliance between the AAP and GFP would be announced.It would be a non-BJP and non-Congress alliance, he said.The state executive of the Goa Forward Party met on Saturday and resolved to immediately move towards an alliance with like-minded secular political forces to unitedly defeat the BJP in the February 2027 Goa Assembly elections.In a social media post, GFP has said "Our message is clear: Goa First. Before party, before politics and before personal ambitions -- Goa First"."This Chovoth (Ganesh Chaturthi), we will strive to give the people of Goa a United Alternative, one that puts Goa first, protects Goemkarponn, and stands firmly against corruption, communalism and the politics of defection," the GFP said.Meanwhile, Goa Congress president Girish Chodankar told reporters here that the GFP has been an ally since 2022 and was still in talks with his party."The Goa Forward Party is in talks with Congress' central leadership for the 2027 Goa Assembly election pre-poll alliance. I have confirmed with my high command even today morning. They have said that the talks for alliance are still on," Chodankar said.The GFP fought the 2022 assembly election in alliance with the Congress, while the AAP had contested on its own. The Sardesai-led party was in talks with the Congress for a pre-poll alliance for the 2027 state elections but had later stalled the discussion, citing no response from the latter.The elections for the Goa legislative assembly are due before March 2027. Article Title: NIA raids 10 locations across Jammu & Kashmir in LeT-linked terror conspiracy case
Article Text:
NIA searches J&K locations to trace LeT handlers’ local support network (file photo)

Investigation began with OGW arrest

NIA examines financial, communication trails

Hafiz Saeed warrant in related terror case

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) on Saturday conducted searches at 10 locations across Jammu and Kashmir in connection with a cross-border terror conspiracy involving Pakistan-based handlers of the proscribed Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) and their alleged network of local Over Ground Workers (OGWs).The searches were carried out in Kupwara, Kulgam, Bandipora, Baramulla and Sopore to gather further evidence related to the conspiracy and ascertain the roles of individuals allegedly providing logistical and other support to infiltrated terrorists, the NIA said.During the searches, incriminating material relevant to the case was seized or secured, according to the agency. The material is being examined and corroborated with other evidence collected during the investigation.The case was initially registered at Police Station Zakoora in Srinagar and was subsequently re-registered by the NIA under Section 23 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967, Sections 7 and 25 of the Arms Act, 1959, and Section 4 of the Explosive Substances Act, 1908.The investigation began after the arrest of an alleged LeT-linked OGW at a naka point during the night of March 31, 2026. A hand grenade and live ammunition were recovered from his possession, the NIA said.Further investigation led to the arrest of Pakistani nationals allegedly linked to the conspiracy and helped investigators identify the suspected roles of members of the local support network.According to the NIA, the investigation so far has revealed links between Pakistan-based LeT handlers and their local associates. These associates were allegedly being used for communication, movement and concealment of infiltrated terrorists, as well as providing shelter, conducting reconnaissance and facilitating other logistical requirements.The agency is also examining the financial trail, communication channels and movement of the accused, along with the source and supply chain of arms and explosives.The objective, according to the NIA, is to establish the complete network and determine the extent of its activities.The latest searches are part of the agency's continuing investigation into the larger conspiracy and the support mechanism allegedly facilitating cross-border terrorism.The NIA said it would continue its investigation to identify all persons involved in the alleged conspiracy and establish their respective roles. Further legal action, including arrests and recoveries, may follow depending on the outcome of the investigation.The searches come amid the NIA's wider investigations into LeT-linked terror networks in Jammu and Kashmir.A Special Court in Jammu on September 8 issued a non-bailable warrant against LeT founder Hafiz Saeed in a terror case related to the alleged supply of weapons, funds and directions to terror groups operating in the Union Territory.It was the second non-bailable warrant issued against Saeed by the Special NIA Court in Jammu in two months.The warrant was issued after the NIA described Saeed, a resident of Sargodha in Pakistan's Punjab province, as an “absconding accused” in a case concerning the arrest of Mohammad Naqeeb Bhat during a check at Pandach on the outskirts of Srinagar earlier this year.A China-made grenade and 15 live rounds were recovered from Bhat, who was booked under the UAPA, Arms Act and Explosive Substances Act.The subsequent investigation led to the alleged busting of a terror network and the arrest of several more terrorists associated with LeT and its offshoot The Resistance Front (TRF), as well as two Pakistani nationals.The NIA told the court that Saeed was allegedly operating from Pakistan and providing weapons, money and directions to terrorists in the Kashmir Valley.The court observed that Saeed's involvement had surfaced during the investigation and that he was “allegedly involved in terrorism”.The latest warrant followed an earlier non-bailable warrant issued against him on July 8 in connection with the Pahalgam terror attack case.
Article Summary: NIA searches J&K locations to trace LeT handlers’ local support network. Investigation began after the arrest of an alleged LeT-linked OGW. A hand grenade and live ammunition were recovered from his possession. NIA said it would continue its investigation to identify all persons involved.
