NEW DELHI: Amruta Fadnavis , wife of Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis , said there was nothing wrong with Muslims participating in Navratri and other festivals, after the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) called for Muslims to be barred from the upcoming Navratri festivities, a demand endorsed by state minister Nitesh Rane.“Festivals are inclusive, and there is nothing wrong with a Muslim person attending the celebrations. If a Muslim also comes and enjoys the festival properly, I do not see anything wrong with it,” Amruta Fadnavis told reporters in Mumbai on Tuesday, PTI reported.Her remarks came in response to a question on Rane’s comments. On Monday, Rane, a BJP colleague of Devendra Fadnavis, backed the VHP, alleging that cases of “love jihad” tend to increase during such festivals. He also called for attendees to undergo identity checks and recite the Hanuman Chalisa before being allowed entry to Navratri events.“Love jihad” is a term used by right-wing activists to allege that Muslim men lure women, mostly from the Hindu community, into relationships with the aim of converting them to Islam.Last week, the VHP announced that Muslims would not be allowed to enter ‘garba’ and ‘dandiya’ venues across Maharashtra during Navratri, which begins on October 11.The VHP has also issued “guidelines” for organisers to verify participants’ identities at Navratri ‘garba’ and ‘dandiya’ events by checking their Aadhaar cards and applying ‘tilak’ on their foreheads.
Article Summary: Amruta Fadnavis said there was nothing wrong with Muslims participating in Navratri and other festivals. The Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) has called for Muslims to be barred from the upcoming festivities. State minister Nitesh Rane backed the VHP, alleging that cases of “love jihad” tend to increase during such festivals.

Article Title: DMK MLAs bundled out as row over Vijay’s remarks rocks Tamil Nadu assembly
Article Text:
Speaker JCD Prabhakar refused to accept DMK's demand to expunge CM Vijay's remark from assembly records

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

CHENNAI: DMK legislators were bundled out of the Tamil Nadu assembly on Tuesday after a stormy confrontation over chief minister C Joseph Vijay’s remarks on late chief minister M Karunanidhi, former Union minister Murasoli Maran, the Sarkaria Commission and ED dossiers relating to cases pending before courts.The dramatic scenes unfolded after speaker J C D Prabhakar refused to expunge Vijay’s remarks, prompting DMK members to raise slogans and staged a sit-in protest on the well of the House. As the protesting members refused to return to their seats despite repeated appeals, the speaker ordered marshals to remove them.The confrontation began during Zero Hour when DMK whip E V Velu raised objections to Vijay’s remarks made during his reply to the demands for grants for the home department on Monday. Velu accused the CM of making baseless allegations and referring to pending cases, saying this went against the traditions of the House.Referring to the Sarkaria Commission, Velu said late chief minister M G Ramachandran was the principal complainant but later told the commission that he had “no idea whatsoever” about the complaint and that it had been drafted by a party functionary, Kannan from Salem. “At the conclusion, Sarkaria made it clear that there was no prima facie case in all the 28 allegations.Therefore, there was no provision for filing any case,” Velu said.He referred to DK leader K Veeramani and Left leaders being booked under MISA, like DMK leader M K Stalin, and said Vijay’s remarks had demeaned their democratic struggle.Ministers Aadhav Arjuna and R Nirmalkumar defended the CM, saying Vijay had referred to the Sarkaria Commission report and other publicly available documents as part of his fight against corruption. They accused the DMK of being the “root of corruption.”Former minister Govi Chezhiaan then posed three questions to the treasury benches: whether the CM could cite ED dossiers as evidence when the cases were pending before courts? whether the Sarkaria Commission could be selectively used for political gains when it had not found anyone guilty of corruption? and why Vijay had chosen to refer to late leaders such as Murasoli Maran?With no response forthcoming from either the treasury benches or the speaker, DMK intensified its protest.The situation turned chaotic after speaker Prabhakar ruled that there was “no need to expunge the CM’s remarks”. He said Vijay had merely referred to the Sarkaria Commission, whose findings had been discussed in the House earlier, and that the CM’s speech was within the rules of the assembly.The ruling triggered a fresh round of protests, with DMK MLAs raising slogans and sitting in the well, keeping the moments tense for nearly 45 minutes, starting from 9.31am and ending at about 10.11am. In between, the speaker also cautioned minister Aadhav Arjuna for his remarks that they would also match the opposition.The speaker repeatedly asked the members to return to their seats and offered to allow Velu and deputy leader of the opposition K N Nehru to speak on the issue. But the DMK members refused to relent.“I will not reverse my ruling,” Prabhakar asserted before directing marshals to remove the protesting MLAs. He cautioned Kallakurichi MLA Vasantham K Karthikeyan against approaching the Chair.Marshals entered the House at about 10.08am and physically removed several MLAs who refused to leave the well, including Kutty alias A Sudhakar of Valparai, Durai Chandrasekaran of Thiruvaiyaru and Vasantham Karthikeyan of Rishivandiyam.Later in the day, Chezhiaan moved a privilege motion against Vijay, accusing the CM of making “baseless allegations” and citing reports connected to cases pending before courts during his reply to the demands for grants for the home department.
Article Summary: Dramatic scenes unfolded after speaker J C D Prabhakar refused to expunge Vijay’s remarks. DMK members raised slogans and staged a sit-in protest on the well of the House. As the protesting members refused to return to their seats, the speaker ordered marshals to remove them.

Article Title: Delhi building collapse: SC appointed amicus curiae seeks safety audit of PGs, hostels across capital
Article Text:
6 killed in Satya Niketan building collapse; FIR against owner

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A Supreme Court-appointed amicus curiae on Wednesday filed a report before the top court on the building collapse in Satya Niketan and requested the apex court to direct its appointed committee to carry out inspections and safety audits of all PG accommodations, private hostels and similar student-accommodation establishments situated in and around colleges and universities across Delhi.Senior advocate Ajit Kumar Sinha, in his report, said that the Satya Niketan incident assumes significance as the locality had witnessed another building collapse in April 2022, in which two people were killed and four injured.“The present incident is also required to be viewed in the context of an earlier building collapse in Satya Niketan in April 2022, in which two persons lost their lives, and four others were injured. The recurrence of such an incident in the same locality raises serious concerns regarding the effectiveness of the existing mechanism for inspection, identification of dangerous structures, and enforcement of building bye-laws”, the amicus report said.He also noted that construction-related work was being undertaken in or around the basement and that there were reports of waterlogging in the basement immediately before the latest collapse.The amicus has sought a time-bound inspection and safety audit of PGs, private hostels and similar student-accommodation establishments around colleges and universities across Delhi, including checks on sanctioned building plans, actual construction and number of floors, basement construction and alterations, land use, structural and fire safety, ingress and egress, and dangerous or ruinous conditions.This comes after seven people were killed when a building collapsed in Satya Niketan on Sunday.Meanwhile, Municipal Corporation of Delhi also directed its executive engineers (building) across all zones to inspect structures under their jurisdiction and submit comprehensive reports by September 10, following the deadly building collapse in south Delhi's Satya Niketan, which killed seven people, officials said.Officials said the information collected during the inspections would be incorporated into an affidavit to be filed before the Delhi High Court within 10 days.The inspections and submission of reports will be personally monitored and supervised by the additional commissioners concerned in each zone, according to the order, they added.
Article Summary: A Supreme Court-appointed amicus curiae filed a report before the top court on the building collapse in Satya Niketan. He requested the apex court to direct its appointed committee to carry out inspections and safety audits of all PG accommodations, private hostels and similar student-accommodation establishments situated in and around colleges and universities.

Article Title: After Trump renamed Lake Ontario 'Lake America,' a Pennsylvania Republican now wants Lake Erie renamed 'Lake Pennsylvania'
Article Text:
David Maloney, Trump

Why Maloney wants Lake Erie renamed

Where the name Lake Erie comes from

Would 'Lake Pennsylvania' become official?

President Donald Trump ’s decision to rename Lake Ontario as “Lake America” has now been followed by a similar proposal involving another Great Lake. A Republican lawmaker in Pennsylvania is preparing a resolution seeking to rename Lake Erie as “Lake Pennsylvania”.State Representative David Maloney argues that the state has a strong economic and cultural connection with the Great Lake. He is expected to urge President Donald Trump, Congress and Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum to take steps towards changing the lake’s name, according to a an official statement issued by him, Newsweek reported.Maloney represents Pennsylvania’s 130th Legislative District in Berks County. He said Pennsylvanians regularly travel to Lake Erie for boating, fishing and family visits, with visitors spending money along the state’s shoreline. He also referred to research by Pennsylvania Sea Grant and said Pennsylvania stocked almost 500,000 yearling steelhead in 2025, which he said was about 40% of the steelhead stocked across the lake.The proposal comes about two weeks after Trump signed an executive order directing US federal agencies to use the name “Lake America” for Lake Ontario.Trump signed the order on August 27, during growing tensions between the United States and Canada over trade. The order requires US federal agencies to use the new name on maps, documents and databases.The Lake Ontario decision itself has faced resistance in Canada and parts of the United States. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney rejected the name change, saying the lake’s name comes from the language of the Indigenous Wendat people and predates both Canadian Confederation and the US Declaration of Independence. Several US governors in the Great Lakes region also dismissed the move.Maloney said Pennsylvania has a particular connection with Lake Erie, which borders the state. He pointed to recreation and fishing as reasons for the proposed name change.“Ohio has plenty of shoreline. New York already has two Great Lakes. Canada has four others,” Maloney said.His office told Newsweek that the proposal is based on how Pennsylvanians care for the lake and how residents of other states also visit it for recreation and fishing. “Be proud and own it,” the office said.Lake Erie is shared by the United States and Canada. Ontario lies along its northern shore, while Michigan, Ohio, Pennsylvania and New York border it on the American side. It is the smallest Great Lake by volume and the shallowest.According to the Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes and Energy, the name comes from the Indigenous people who lived along its southern shore when Europeans reached the area in the early 1600s.“Erie” is a shortened form of the Iroquoian word “Erielhonan”, which means “long tail” and refers to the eastern cougar,The National Museum of the Great Lakes says Europeans discovered Lake Erie last among the Great Lakes. Control of the lake was also strategically important because it provided access to areas above Niagara Falls.Maloney’s proposal would face the same broader issue surrounding any US attempt to change the name of a body of water shared with another country.The US Board on Geographic Names says proposals to change existing geographic names require a compelling reason and evidence of support. The board generally discourages changes to existing names.If the federal government approved the change, “Lake Pennsylvania” would become the name used by US federal departments and agencies. But Canada has its own geographical naming authorities, so a US decision would not automatically change the lake’s official name in Canada.The proposal is still at an early stage. Maloney circulated a co-sponsorship memo on September 9 and said he plans to introduce a resolution asking Trump, Congress and Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum to begin the renaming process. As of September 9, the measure had not been formally introduced in the Pennsylvania House. That means “Lake Pennsylvania” remains only a proposal for now, with several political and administrative steps still required before any official US name change could take effect.
Article Summary: State Representative David Maloney argues that the state has a strong economic and cultural connection with the Great Lake. Maloney represents Pennsylvania’s 130th Legislative District in Berks County. He said Pennsylvanians regularly travel to Lake Erie for boating, fishing and family visits, with visitors spending money along the state's shoreline.

Article Title: Indonesia launches search for 140 after ship carrying over 240 loses contact
Article Text:
The Virgo Transport 8 was travelling from Surabaya in East Java to Banjarmasin (Representative image)

Search continues for missing passengers

A passenger ship carrying 243 people lost contact in the Java Sea early Sunday while travelling from Indonesia’s East Java province to South Kalimantan, with 102 people rescued, one person dead and a search underway for 140 others.The Virgo Transport 8 was reported missing after encountering bad weather during its journey from Surabaya to Banjarmasin. Indonesian rescuers launched a major search operation after the vessel’s operator alerted authorities.The ship departed Surabaya at 10:13am local time on Saturday and was travelling towards Banjarmasin when contact was lost at around 2am on Sunday, according to Indonesia’s search and rescue agency.Rescue teams have so far recovered 102 people from the vessel, while one person has died. Authorities are continuing the search for 140 people who remain unaccounted for.The Search and Rescue Office in Banjarmasin said it received the report about two hours after contact was lost. I Putu Sudayana, who heads the agency, said the operator had informed authorities after receiving information that the ship had encountered bad weather.The vessel’s last known position was about 148 km (92 miles) from a pier in Banjarmasin. Rescue teams were deployed towards the area, with authorities coordinating with maritime agencies and other relevant bodies.Sudayana said authorities were mobilising available personnel and assets given the large number of people aboard, while continuing to monitor weather conditions in the area.Indonesia, an archipelago of about 17,000 islands, relies heavily on ferries and passenger ships for transport, particularly because sea travel is often more affordable and accessible than air travel. However, safety standards have not always been rigorously enforced, contributing to a relatively high rate of maritime accidents.
Article Summary: The Virgo Transport 8 was travelling from Surabaya in East Java to Banjarmasin. It was reported missing after encountering bad weather during its journey. Rescuers have so far recovered 102 people from the vessel, while one person has died.

Article Title: ‘Slipped and fell’ on saleswoman, then kissed her twice: Mumbai man gets 1-year jail
Article Text:
AI Generated Image Used For Representational Purpose Only

‘Enough proof that act was intentional’





MUMBAI: Ruling that a natural reaction to a fall does not involve kissing the victim, a sessions court convicted and sentenced to one year rigorous imprisonment a 34-year-old cleaner who claimed he ac­cidentally “slipped and fe­ll” onto a saleswoman at a Borivli (W) mall be­fore forcibly kissing her twice last year.In a trial that lasted only 2 months, dismissing the defence, the court found Ritesh Armulla guilty of using criminal force and making unwelcome physical contact with explicit sexual overtures.“Even for the sake of arg­ument, if it is considered a pe­r­son slipped and fell on an­ot­h­er person, the natural re­ac­ti­on would be different fr­om the person kissing the person on whom he fell,” judge said.The offences are covered under Sections 74, assault or use of criminal force against a woman with intent to outrage, or knowing it is likely to outrage, her modesty, and 75, sexual harassment, of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.Additional Sessions Judge P A Sane said the victim’s evidence was “convincing” and not disbelievable. “There is nothing coming on record as to why the victim will depose against the accused. Moreover, it is coming on record that she did not know the accused before the incident. So there is no possibility that she would falsely involve the accused in this case,” the judge held.This is one of the few convictions since the BNS replaced the IPC.The court sentenced Armulla to one year’s RI and a fine of Rs 1,000 under Section 74, and one year’s simple imprisonment and a fine of Rs 500 under Section 75. Both sentences will run concurrently. The judge said there was sufficient reason to believe that the accused intentionally kissed the complainant, made her fall and kissed her again, amounting to outraging modesty by criminal force. He had followed her on the pretext of being shown the washroom and physically contacted her with explicit sexual overtures.The case arose from an incident on Sept 17, 2025, at a mall in Borivli West. The victim, a sales girl at the mall, told the court that around 6 pm she was on duty and walking towards billing counter number 6 after taking a cold drink bottle. A man in a pink shirt approached her and asked where the washroom was. She pointed in that direction, but he repeatedly asked her to show him.According to the prosecution, after she asked him to go ahead, he left briefly and returned. The victim said the accused came from behind, knocked against her, asked her to take him to the washroom and, when she refused and proceeded towards the billing counter, forcibly kissed her, caused her to fall and kissed her again. Staff and other people in the mall caught him. Police were called, and he was taken into custody the same day.The FIR was lodged immediately. Police prepared the spot panchnama, arrested Armulla, recorded statements and collected CCTV footage. The chargesheet was filed on November 11, 2025, and charges were framed on July 4, 2026.The prosecution examined the victim, an eyewitness, the investigating officer and a mall employee linked to the CCTV footage. The victim identified Armulla in court, and the eyewitness supported her account.The defence questioned proof of the CCTV footage, non-examination of a mall official, absence of hash value and intent, claiming any contact may have been accidental. The court found the oral evidence sufficient and granted set-off for custody already undergone since arrest.
Article Summary: Ritesh Armulla, 34, found guilty of using criminal force and making unwelcome physical contact with explicit sexual overtures. Court ruled that a natural reaction to a fall does not involve kissing the victim. Court sentenced Armulla to one year’s RI and a fine of Rs 1,000 under Section 74.

Article Title: Kulbhushan Bharadwaj: Man who led namaz protests in Gurgaon is new Bar president
Article Text:
Bharadwaj has been associated with several contentious lawyer protests. (Image Credit: X)





GURGAON: Kulbhushan Bharadwaj, who led repeated protests against namaz being offered in public places in the city, was elected president of the District Bar Association Friday. Bharadwaj, a long-time associate of RSS and its affiliates, defeated Vinod Rao by 244 votes.Bharadwaj polled 1,834 votes against Rao’s 1,590 in a six-way contest. A total of 4,963 votes were counted. His victory also ended the prolonged dominance of Yadav candidates in the Bar president’s post, where community mobilisation had traditionally played a key role.Bharadwaj has been associated with several contentious lawyer protests. During an anti-namaz agitation in 2021, an FIR was registered after he allegedly led a rally on an excavator, carrying a sword, through Sadar Bazaar. He later joined lawyers protesting against judicial officer Roopam over alleged misbehaviour. The agitation saw Bharadwaj and others lock the court gate and disrupt proceedings.His election campaign also drew support from RSS and affiliated organisations, which urged members to vote for him, according to people familiar with the mobilisation.The election came amid recurring friction between lawyers and judges in the city. Bharadwaj said his priority would be to improve relations and court infrastructure. “I will try to live up to the expectation of the members and stress on improving coordination between judges and lawyers and work to improve the infrastructure inside the court premises,” he said.Manish Shandilya, general secretary of Adhivakta Parishad Gurgaon and a senior Bar member, said the new body must bridge the divide. “We hope the new body will ensure coordination between Bar and Bench and take along everyone irrespective of their affiliation,” he said. He added that lawyers must receive due respect when they raise concerns. Bharadwaj’s 244-vote margin gave him a clear mandate in a contest involving six candidates, but his election also puts the focus on whether the new leadership can ease long-running tensions inside the district court.
Article Summary: Kulbhushan Bharadwaj is a long-time associate of RSS and its affiliates. He defeated Vinod Rao by 244 votes in a six-way contest. His election campaign also drew support from RSS and affiliated organisations. The election came amid recurring friction between lawyers and judges.

Article Title: 'Minimum infra, deviation from syllabus': West Bengal shuts down 252 madrasas, sends show-cause notices to 100
Article Text:
The 252 madrasas that have been served closure notices are devoid of minimum infrastructure.

By: Soumitra.Nandi

2,396 functioning without registration

Deviation from syllabus, lack of classroom space among issues





KOLKATA: The state minority affairs and madrasa education department has sent closure notices to 252 madrasas across the state and issued show-cause notices to about 100 others following a survey of unaided madrasas.“The 252 madrasas that have been served closure notices are devoid of minimum infrastructure. The 100-odd that have been issued show-cause will have to respond and and if their replies are found to be unsatisfactory, we will take action against them too. We want madrasa students to pursue modern, mainstream education and shine in life just like students from other schools,” said Kshudiram Tudu, minister-in-charge of the department.Malda leads the list of closures with around 44-45 madrasas while North Dinajpur is second with around 37, followed by 32-odd in South 24 Parganas and about 25 each in Murshidabad and Nadia.The action followed a field verification through the district administration of all madrasas, with particular focus on Khariji madrasas. The aim was to identify madrasas functioning without authorisation and ensure compliance with regulatory framework.Khariji madrasas are independent Islamic schools that operate without govt funding, formal recognition or regulatory control. They rely entirely on public donations and charitable trusts.The magistrates of all 22 districts and the Kolkata area submitted reports on madrasas functioning within their respective jurisdictions. Detailed information relating to registration status, management, student enrolment and identity, teaching staff, infrastructure and sources of funding were collected and scrutinised.The DMs reported that about 2,132 madrasas were functioning with proper registration/affiliation etc, while 2,396 were functioning without the required registration/affiliation from any govt or board. The department deputed dedicated inspection/investigation teams from the state level for re-verification of the reports received to ascertain that correctness of information furnished by the institutions corresponded with the actual position on the ground.The infrastructural lacunae at the madrasas included non-availability of classroom space, inadequate students or teachers, stark deviation from standard state school syllabus or administrative rules.According to a senior Nabanna official, state govt found that in a good number of Khariji madrasas, anti-India education was being imparted and innocent students were being brainwashed, that has prompted the survey exercise. The department will continue the verification and enforcement exercise and take strict, evidence-based and legally sustainable action against institutions found to be unauthorised or non-compliant.
Article Summary: Malda leads the list of closures with around 44-45 madrasas. North Dinajpur is second with around 37, followed by 32-odd in South 24 Parganas. About 25 each in Murshidabad and Nadia.

Article Title: ABVP-backed candidates win University College union polls; NSUI demands action against principal
Article Text:
University College, Mangalore students with the ABVP hold election win rally in Mangaluru on Saturday





MANGALURU: ABVP-backed candidates won all 37 posts in the Students’ Union elections at University College, Mangalore on Friday, even as the NSUI alleged that the polls were conducted in violation of the state govt’s guidelines.NSUI Dakshina Kannada division convener Suhan Alva said the organisation opposed the elections being held without clear directions from the govt. He alleged that NSUI learnt only on Tuesday that the college had decided to conduct the elections on Friday.“When the govt has said there will be direct elections, why was this election conducted? We have not received any instructions,” Alva said.He said NSUI representatives had approached the university vice-chancellor, the district minister and the college principal, urging them to follow the govt guidelines. Alva claimed that the district minister had contacted the higher education secretary, who reportedly said that any election conducted without following the govt order would not be valid.Alva also alleged that the VC had earlier assured them that the election would not be held. “Everything was done despite this. We will condemn the election and demand that it be declared invalid and reconducted once the govt issues clear guidelines.We also demand strict action against the college principal,” he said.He said general elections for student representatives had been announced after nearly three decades, and that several students were keen to contest. “We had been waiting for this opportunity. There was enough time to conduct the process properly,” he said.The NSUI will seek an appointment with the chief minister during his visit to Mangaluru for the cabinet meeting and urge the govt to conduct student elections in accordance with the guidelines, Alva said.Meanwhile, ABVP Dakshina Kannada division convener Suvith Shetty said the election was conducted peacefully on Friday. Polling began at 10 am, followed by a victory procession after the results were announced.The procession started from the college premises and passed through Clock Tower and Town Hall. Participants paid floral tribute to the statue of BR Ambedkar before the procession concluded around 3 pm.Shetty said the procession passed off without any untoward incident. He also said that neither Alva nor his supporters were present during the procession despite the NSUI’s opposition to the election.The college has around 1,650 students. Shetty claimed that nearly 90% of the students supported the ABVP, while around 10% supported the NSUI. According to him, all 37 elected candidates were backed by the ABVP, with candidates from no other student organisation winning a post.The elected office bearers include Srajan, president; Akshay R, secretary; Ranjitha HI, joint secretary; Charan, Fine Arts Association secretary; and Shravya N Shetty, Fine Arts Association joint secretary.
Article Summary: NSUI Dakshina Kannada division convener Suhan Alva said the organisation opposed the elections being held without clear directions from the govt. He alleged that NSUI learnt only on Tuesday that the college had decided to conduct the elections on Friday.

Article Title: Why was YouTuber Brandon Buckingham arrested? The alleged auto theft charge and latest details explained
Article Text:
Brandon Buckingham reportedly booked on theft of auto charge

I Almost Died in Chicago...

The King of Kensington...

Searching for the Most Wanted Driver in America

Brandon Buckingham’s official X account says “Free Brandon”

YouTuber Brandon Buckingham is at the center of fresh controversy after reports claimed he was arrested in Louisiana on an alleged auto theft charge. A mugshot and booking notice circulating online have fueled the reports, while his official X account has responded with a brief message calling for his release. However, details surrounding the reported arrest remain limited, and the allegations have not been independently confirmed beyond the documents and posts cited in the reports.The reported arrest surfaced on September 11 after industry reporter @Awk20000 shared what appeared to be Buckingham’s mugshot alongside a booking notice. According to the report, the 31-year-old YouTuber was booked by the Washington Parish Sheriff's Office on a charge listed as “Theft of Auto/Vehicle.”The post stated:"Brandon Buckingham was arrested on alleged Theft of Auto/Vehicle."The reported booking information also claimed that Buckingham had not been assigned a bond at the time."Brandon Buckingham (age 31 with no address listed) was booked on the charge of Theft of Auto/Vehicle by the Washington Parish Sheriff's Office. No bond set at this time."The wording is important because the available information describes an alleged charge, not a conviction.No further details about the circumstances behind the reported case, including what vehicle may be involved or what allegedly happened, were provided in the source material.Buckingham has built his audience by putting himself in unusual and often unpredictable situations. His videos frequently take him into controversial communities and difficult environments, giving his work a documentary feel rather than following the format of conventional creator content.His channel has grown to more than 1.3 million subscribers. Among his notable projects areandThe reported arrest comes after Buckingham returned to regular content creation earlier this year following a serious health crisis in late 2025.The situation gained another layer of attention when Buckingham’s official X account appeared to respond directly to the reports.The account posted a short message:"Free Brandon."It later added another statement in the comments, linking the reported arrest to the creator’s broader approach to journalism and content."Legalize Journalism. Buy a mugshot T-shirt and support Brandon’s release from jail."The account also promoted merchandise featuring Buckingham’s mugshot, with proceeds presented as a way to support his release.Buckingham’s arrest report has quickly attracted attention because of the nature of his work. His videos often involve direct encounters, travel and investigations into people or places that attract controversy online. That style has helped him develop a reputation for going beyond the usual boundaries of creator content.Still, the most significant details remain unclear. The reports currently circulating do not establish the full circumstances of the alleged theft charge, and the available material does not provide a court outcome or confirmation of what happens next.For now, Buckingham’s reported legal situation remains developing, with his supporters publicly calling for his release while questions remain about the case and the allegations behind the booking.
Article Summary: Brandon Buckingham reportedly booked on theft of auto charge. His official X account has responded with a brief message calling for his release. Details surrounding the reported arrest remain limited, and allegations have not been independently confirmed beyond the documents and posts cited in the reports.

Article Title: 'In-laws may kill me': Noida woman’s call to brother before husband pushes her to death from terrace over dowry
Article Text:
She feared for her life





NOIDA: A man was arrested for allegedly pushing his wife to death from the terrace of their two-storey Muradnagar home over unmet dowry demands of Rs 30 lakh in cash and a car. Four other members of the family named in the case are yet to be arrested.Akriti, a Bhangel resident, had married Gaurav of Muradnagar around six months ago. Her family said the couple were initially due to marry on Feb 20, but the wedding was called off after Gaurav’s family allegedly raised additional dowry demands. The two sides later reached a compromise at Muradnagar police station.The family alleged Akriti and Gaurav subsequently married without informing their relatives and began living together in Muradnagar. They said the demand for Rs 30 lakh and a car continued after the marriage.On the night of Sept 7, Akriti called her brother Prabhat and allegedly told him she was being assaulted and feared her in-laws might kill her. Soon after, Gaurav allegedly called Prabhat and said Akriti had fallen from the terrace.Akriti was taken to hospital, but died from her injuries on Sept 10. Her family alleged she had been deliberately thrown from the terrace over the dowry dispute.An FIR under relevant BNS sections and provisions of the Dowry Act was registered at Muradnagar police station against Gaurav, his father Ramesh, mother Saroj and sisters Soni and Neha, all residents of Main Road Colony.An ACP of Masuri circle said while Gaurav was arrested, teams were conducting raids to trace the other accused. Police said the allegations and circumstances surrounding Akriti’s fall were being investigated and further action would depend on evidence collected during the probe.
Article Summary: Akriti, a Bhangel resident, had married Gaurav of Muradnagar around six months ago. Her family said the couple were initially due to marry on Feb 20, but the wedding was called off after Gaurv’s family allegedly raised additional dowry demands. Four other members of the family named in the case are yet to be arrested.

Article Title: Debt, poison and one blow each: New chilling details in Jaipur quadruple murder
Article Text:
Mounting debt emerging as a possible motive behind murders





JAIPUR: Police investigating the Kardhani quadruple murder suspect that accused Rahul Jha (45) may have incapacitated his wife and three daughters with poison or sedatives before killing them with a single blow each to the head. “He attacked all victims with a single blow to their heads, as opposed to multiple blows,” said an officer.Froth was found around victims’ mouths, prompting investigators to examine whether a poisonous substance or sedative mixed with food was given to them. Police, however, said frothing can also occur in cases of severe blunt-force trauma to the head, and therefore it is not conclusive evidence of poisoning.Investigators are also piecing together a possible sequence of events inside the house. Police suspect Rahul may have checked on the four after they fell unconscious and realised they were still alive. He may then have used a roughly 10kg cinder block to deliver a blow to each victim’s head.Police are investigating whether Rahul planned the killings, citing findings that each victim appeared to have suffered a single major blow rather than repeated attacks in a fit of rage.Mounting debt is emerging as a possible motive. Investigators have learnt that Rahul’s wife, Geeta, was also named as a partner in the ownership documents of the house. One line of inquiry is whether Rahul wanted to mortgage the property to raise money to clear his debts and whether Geeta had opposed the move.Police have announced a reward of Rs 25,000 for information leading to Rahul’s arrest. Multiple teams are tracking his movements through CCTV footage and other evidence.
Article Summary: Rahul Jha may have incapacitated his wife and three daughters with poison or sedatives before killing them with a single blow each to the head. Mounting debt is emerging as a possible motive. Police have announced a reward of Rs 25,000 for information leading to Rahul’s arrest.

Article Title: Veteran Congress leader and socialist thinker Ratnakar Mahajan dies at 80 in Pune
Article Text:
Senior Congress leader Dr Ratnakar Mahajan passed away in Pune on Saturday





PUNE: Senior Congress leader , socialist thinker and political analyst Dr Ratnakar Mahajan died at his residence in Pune on Saturday following a brief illness, his close associates said. He was 80.Mahajan had been unwell for the past few days, according to his associates. His last rites will be performed at the Vaikunth Smashanbhoomi in Pune later on Saturday, news agency PTI reported.Mahajan hailed from Indapur taluka and moved to Pune to pursue higher education. He later became associated with several social and political movements, working on social causes through organisations including the Yuvak Kranti Dal, Rashtra Seva Dal and Bharat Jodo Abhiyan, besides student movements.After joining the Congress , Mahajan served as the spokesperson of the party's Maharashtra unit. He also served as the editor of*'Shidori' magazine.Mahajan was known for his engagement with socialist thought, political analysis and social movements over the course of his public life.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Mahajan had been unwell for the past few days, according to his associates. His last rites will be performed at the Vaikunth Smashanbhoomi in Pune later on Saturday. Mahajan hailed from Indapur taluka and moved to Pune to pursue higher education.

Article Title: Gurgaon waterlogging has direct bearing on human rights: HHRC
Article Text:
A school bus stranded on a flooded Subhas Chowk stretch on Aug 26

TOI





GURGAON: Recurring waterlogging in Gurgaon is not merely a civic inconvenience but has a direct bearing on citizens’ human rights, Haryana Human Rights Commission (HHRC) has observed. Taking suo motu cognisance of TOI reports, the commission ordered govt agencies to conduct a comprehensive audit of the city’s drainage and civic infrastructure.In an order published Friday, the commission noted that the problem appeared to have persisted over several years and, therefore, could not be attributed to one wet spell. Such repeated disruption of roads, schools, emergency services, water supply and everyday mobility during heavy rain could not be treated as an “unavoidable feature of urban life”, it said.Drainage was a “basic and essential prerequisite” of planned urban development, HHRC said, linking its failure with Article 21 of Constitution, which guarantees the right to life and personal liberty, including living with dignity in conditions conducive to health and safety. It also referred to the constitutional obligations related to public health and environmental protection.The HHRC full bench, comprising Justice (retd) Lalit Batra, judicial member Kuldeep Jain and member Deep Bhatia, stopped short of holding any agency responsible at this stage.It said persistent failure of essential civic infrastructure, “if attributable to neglect, inadequate planning, failure of maintenance or failure to take reasonable preventive measures”, may have a direct bearing on human rights. The proceedings, it said, would ascertain the facts, determine responsibility, and secure preventive and remedial measures.The commission pointed to the ordeal of school students stranded in buses, parents wading through flooded roads, and the difficulties in getting information about children’s safety. It also referred to reports of commuters taking disproportionately long to cover short distances and the disruption to ambulances and essential services during the Aug 24 downpour, reported byThe panel stressed that Gurgaon’s civic infrastructure must match the scale and density of its population and economic activity.The commission ordered GMDA, the municipal corporation, Haryana Shehri Vikas Pradhikaran, PWD, the public health engineering department, the irrigation and water resources department, DHBVN, town planning authorities and the district administration to conduct a technical audit of Gurgaon’s drainage and associated infrastructure.The audit will have to identify the capacity of the existing storm-water network, natural drains and watercourses, chronic waterlogging points (including the 99 locations flagged by authorities), causes of water accumulation, condition of drains and pumping stations, possible interconnection of sewage and storm-water systems, vulnerable underground utilities, and road-level and drainage deficiencies.HHRC further ordered GIS-based mapping of natural and engineered drainage channels and identification of encroachments or obstructions affecting natural drainage. It asked the authorities concerned to assess whether the existing system could cope with present and projected rainfall and future urbanisation.Separately, the commission sought a report on implementation of the SOP on school transport. It called for real-time tracking of school buses; communication between schools, parents, police and the administration; designated safe holding points, and restrictions on school buses entering identified high-risk waterlogging locations during extreme rainfall.It also directed authorities to identify emergency corridors for ambulances, fire services and police, and ordered a vulnerability assessment of roads, culverts, underpasses and underground utilities, particularly around the cave-in reported near IFFCO Chowk.Agencies will have to provide details of drainage deficiencies reported during the last five years, remedial measures sanctioned and the status of their implementation. They must also furnish details of pre-monsoon desilting, pumping capacity, deployment during the Aug 24 rainfall, response times, and the time taken to clear waterlogging at major locations.The commission suggested an independent technical assessment be undertaken by an IIT, NIT or another reputable hydrological/urban infrastructure institution, covering the whole Gurgaon drainage basin rather than examining individual waterlogging spots in isolation.
Article Summary: Recurring waterlogging in Gurgaon is not merely a civic inconvenience but has a direct bearing on citizens’ human rights, Haryana Human Rights Commission (HHRC) has observed. Taking suo motu cognisance of TOI reports, the commission ordered govt agencies to conduct a comprehensive audit of the city’s drainage and civic infrastructure.

Article Title: LeT founder Hafiz Saeed in Pakistan, aiding Kashmir terrorists: NIA; Jammu court issues non-bailable warrant
Article Text:
India's most-wanted terrorist Hafiz Saeed is reportedly in Pakistan, the NIA informed a Jammu court

Hafiz Saeed terror case: How probe led to LeT founder

Jammu court issues second NBW against Hafiz Saeed

Hafiz Saeed's link to Pahalgam terror attack





JAMMU: Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) founder and India's most-wanted terrorist Hafiz Saeed is currently in Pakistan, the National Investigation Agency ( NIA ) told a Special Court in Jammu, which issued a second non-bailable warrant (NBW) against him in two months in connection with a terror case involving the alleged supply of weapons, funds and directions to terror groups operating in Jammu and Kashmir.The NIA moved an application seeking an NBW against Saeed under Section 75 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). The LeT founder, a designated terrorist and resident of Sargodha in Pakistan's Punjab province, has been described as an "absconding accused" in the case.The case relates to the arrest of Mohammad Naqeeb Bhat during a check at Pandach on the outskirts of Srinagar earlier this year. A China-made grenade and 15 live rounds were recovered from Bhat, a resident of Batpora.Bhat was subsequently booked at Zakoora Police Station under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), Arms Act and Explosive Substances Act.Further investigation into the case led to the busting of a terror network and the arrest of several more terrorists allegedly associated with LeT and its offshoot, The Resistance Front (TRF), along with two Pakistani nationals.According to the NIA, Saeed's alleged involvement emerged during the investigation.The agency said the arrested Pakistani terrorists were allegedly associated with him."Saeed is operating from Pakistan and providing weapons, money and directions to terrorists operating in the Kashmir Valley. The information is gathered that the said terrorist at present is in Pakistan and deliberately evading his arrest to escape the clutches of law," the NIA told the court.After hearing the NIA's submissions, Special Judge under the NIA Act Prem Sagar on September 8 observed that Saeed's involvement had emerged during the investigation and that he was "allegedly involved in terrorism."The court also noted that Saeed was at large and that the investigating agency had been unable to secure his attendance "in the ordinary manner". It subsequently issued a general non-bailable warrant against him.The latest warrant is the second NBW issued against Saeed by the Special NIA Court in Jammu in two months.Earlier, on July 8, the same court had issued an NBW against Saeed in connection with the Pahalgam terror attack in April, in which 25 tourists and a local resident were killed.Saeed is the founder of the proscribed LeT and a designated terrorist.The latest proceedings relate to the separate terror case involving the alleged supply of weapons, funds and directions to terror operatives in the Union Territory.(With PTI inputs)
Article Summary: India's most-wanted terrorist Hafiz Saeed is reportedly in Pakistan, the NIA informed a Jammu court. The LeT founder, a designated terrorist, has been described as an "absconding accused" in the case. The case relates to the arrest of Mohammad Naqeeb Bhat during a check at Pandach.

Article Title: Rape convict ex-MP Prajwal Revanna's smuggled jail phone contained multiple pornographic videos: Police
Article Text:
During the inspection, a prohibited mobile phone, SIM card, charger and notebook were found in a cell.





BENGALURU: Multiple pornographic videos were found on a mobile phone seized from jailed former Janata Dal (Secular) MP Prajwal Revanna , police sources told TOI on Saturday.Revanna, the former Hassan MP who is currently serving a sentence after being convicted in a sexual assault case, allegedly received a mobile phone, SIM card, charger and pen drive in a coordinated smuggling operation involving five others, including a jail staffer, police said.All five people have been arrested in connection with the case, police said.Investigators said Revanna allegedly paid Rs 70,000 to have the mobile phone smuggled into the prison and another Rs 30,000 for the SIM card.Jail warden Prakash Gawade allegedly handed the phone to Revanna personally. Undertrial prisoner Mohammed Tausif, who is accused in the DJ Halli case, allegedly concealed the SIM card in his mouth and passed it to Revanna, police said.Gawade allegedly handed over the charger and pen drive to Revanna during subsequent visits, investigators said. The jail staffer had previously been arrested and suspended on charges of allegedly smuggling ganja into the prison.In August, Central Crime Branch officers raided Revanna’s barrack and seized the mobile phone, SIM card, charger and pen drive. An FIR was subsequently registered against Revanna and his co-inmate Pratap Rai.Rai, however, denied any involvement, saying Revanna had been using the mobile phone even before Rai joined him in the barrack.“While Naveen and Siddiqui arranged the phone and the Sim, Manjunath connected these men with Prajwal and Gawde. The four private persons and Prajwal said that besides paying money for mobile and Sim, they paid Rs 1 lakh (Rs 70,000 for mobile and Rs 30,000 for Sim) to Gawde,” an investigating officer told TOI.
Article Summary: Multiple pornographic videos were found on a mobile phone seized from jailed former Janata Dal (Secular) MP Prajwal Revanna. Revanna allegedly paid Rs 70,000 to have the mobile phone smuggled into the prison and another Rs 30,000 for the SIM card. Five people have been arrested in connection with the case.

Article Title: 'Only tea was good': Near Jantar Mantar, Sonam Wangchuk appeals for support to Ladakh’s fight for democracy
Article Text:
Sonam Wangchuk

Poll Vote & Share your view What should be the top priority for Ladakh’s future governance? Democratic representation Protection of land rights Safeguarding local culture Protecting the environment 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





SRINAGAR: Leh Apex Body (LAB) member and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk early Saturday appealed to people across the country to support Ladakh’s fight for democracy, saying the Centre had failed to give Ladakhi leaders an assurance at the September 9 meeting that major decisions concerning land allotment and local governance would not be taken by the current administration until a democratic government was formed in the Union Territory.The founder of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), Abhijeet Dipke, supported Wangchuk, stating, “Stand with Ladakh!”“Hello friends, cockroaches, how are you? I am in Delhi and right next to the place where we spent weeks with you all, starving, yes, Jantar Mantar. But don’t worry. I am not here for any protest or fast. We came here from Ladakh for a meeting with the Home Ministry for a dialogue. The meeting has been going on for the preservation of the culture, nature and land of Ladakh, and this meeting was also part of it,” Wangchuk said in a message posted on social media early Saturday.Wangchuk shared a video of famous comedian Jaspal Bhatti, saying the meeting resulted in no new steps except fixing the date for the next meeting.“Only tea was good in the meeting, otherwise no new decision was made,” he said. He said decisions already taken, including the creation of a democratic structure in Ladakh under an assembly, were repeated. But he said the government did not provide any assurance that the process of the proposed Assembly would not be undermined by major decisions taken by the local administration and the office of the lieutenant governor in Ladakh.“We had only expected a small, legitimate assurance from the government that until a democratic structure is established in Ladakh, the UT administration should not take any major decisions that would change the face of Ladakh, whether it is land allotment or local governance. No major changes should be brought in these areas and it should be done in coordination with the democratic structure.”Wangchuk said if they get an assurance from the government within a week on the issue, they will celebrate the padyatra from September 19 to September 24 as “a memorial padyatra of the martyrs who sacrificed their lives for Ladakh.”“Otherwise, we will make it a big demonstration on behalf of the people of the entire country that justice should be done to Ladakh,” he said, adding that, as in every other state in the country, major decisions should be left to the people.On September 9, the Leh Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance, the two organisations negotiating with the Union government for administrative autonomy for Ladakh, held talks with the MHA’s subcommittee in Delhi.After the talks, chief secretary of Ladakh Ashish Kundra said the Centre had agreed to have a legislative body under Article 371 in the region, but it would require a constitutional amendment with a two-thirds majority in Parliament.“There was a discussion on whether there would be direct or indirect elections of the UT legislative body through the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils. Representatives of LAB and KDA said elections should be direct and a consensus was reached on this issue,” Kundra said at a press conference in Leh. “The question that remains to be answered concerns the relationship between the LAHDCs and the UT-level body. What powers will be vested in LAHDCs and what will be the jurisdiction of the UT-level body?”The chief secretary said the Centre had handed the Ladakh groups a list of eight to 10 questions to which they did not have immediate answers. “They were requested to think about those, consult the public and tell us what they think, so that we can move towards a draft by taking these issues forward at the next meeting in October,” he said.The chief secretary said the Centre did not want to impose any administrative model that was not acceptable to the people. “We want to move forward only after discussion with everyone. When in good faith and in the interest of everyone, everything is moving forward, it is the responsibility of the leadership here to create an environment of positivity among people, to give them hope that things are moving forward.”In a joint statement after the meeting, the LAB and KDA said the meeting furthered the “in-principle understanding” reached during talks on May 22 and July 3 on Ladakh’s demands, including constitutional safeguards through special provisions under Article 371. They said the MHA stopped short of guaranteeing powers across the board under Lists II and III of the Seventh Schedule, including law and order.The groups, however, expressed concern about “developments taking place with respect to formation of new districts, creation of hill councils of each of the new districts, and other” major irreversible changes being made before an elected body at the Union Territory level.LAB and KDA said they unanimously opposed what they called “irreversible changes” being made to the administrative and political setup of Ladakh before the UT-level body was formed.Ladakhi representatives have been in talks with the MHA since 2023 for safeguards covering land, jobs, culture and the environment. The MHA set up the committee on January 2, 2023, but the process stalled after four people were killed and more than 80 injured in alleged police firing on protesters demanding statehood in Leh in September last year.Wangchuk was accused of inciting the protesters. He was arrested, charged under the NSA and kept in Jodhpur jail. The Centre revoked his NSA detention in March this year. After his release, Wangchuk participated in the May 22 talks with the Centre. He was also one of the LAB representatives at the September 9 talks.
Article Summary: Leh Apex Body member and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk appealed to people across the country to support Ladakh’s fight for democracy. He said the Centre had failed to give Ladakhi leaders an assurance at the September 9 meeting that major decisions concerning land allotment and local governance would not be taken.

Article Title: Shia cleric Yasoob Abbas meets Iranian President Pezeshkian, calls for stronger India-Iran ties
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Maulana Yasoob Abbas, general secretary of the All India Shia Personal Law Board, met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in New Delhi and called for strengthening ties between India and Iran, his office said in a statement.Abbas welcomed Pezeshkian on behalf of the Shia community in India and handed him a letter seeking closer bilateral relations. He said India and Iran were ancient civilisations with longstanding cultural, intellectual, spiritual and trade links.According to the statement, Abbas sought greater cooperation between the two countries in education, trade, culture, science, technology, connectivity and energy. He expressed hope that bilateral relations would strengthen further under Pezeshkian's leadership.The Shia cleric also raised concerns over tensions in West Asia and called for de-escalation and restoration of peace and stability in the region.Abbas expressed grief over the reported death of Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and condemned the killing of children, teachers and other civilians in an alleged attack on Shajareh Tayyebeh Elementary School in Minab.He also condemned terrorism, extremism and violence, saying the Indian Shia community stood for peace, dialogue, humanity and justice.Abbas expressed hope for peace, reconstruction and progress in Iran and said the historical relationship between India and Iran should be further expanded in the coming yearsSeparately, Maulana Kalbe Jawad Naqvi, general secretary of the Majlis-e-Ulama-e-Hind, met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian at a programme hosted in his honour at Delhi’s Oberoi hotel, according to a statement issued by Naqvi’s office. Naqvi congratulated Pezeshkian and paid tribute to the courage, resistance and sacrifices of the Iranian people in confronting oppressive forces.During his address, Naqvi spoke about Iran’s growing regional influence and called for further strengthening the friendly ties between India and Iran. He said closer cooperation between the two countries reflected the aspirations of their people. Several prominent personalities from different fields attended the programme.
Article Summary: Maulana Yasoob Abbas, general secretary of the All India Shia Personal Law Board, met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian. Abbas sought greater cooperation between the two countries in education, trade, culture, science, technology, connectivity and energy.

Article Title: Thousands in Texas were left without internet and TV after outage; Iranian hackers say we did it; AT&T says: No, we ...
Article Text:
AT&T outage reports reached nearly 6,000

What AT&T says

Hackers warn of more attacks

AT&T outage reports reached nearly 6,000

Thousands of users in Texas were left without internet, TV and phone services after an AT&T outage on Monday, September 7. An Iranian-linked hacking group later claimed responsibility for the disruption. The group, APT IRAN, said on Telegram that it had attacked telecommunications and other critical infrastructure in Texas. It also claimed responsibility for disrupting an unnamed water utility in the state. The claim was first reported by Threat Beat, a publication associated with the McCrary Institute for Cyber and Critical Infrastructure Security at Auburn University.According to Threat Beat, APT IRAN is closely linked to CyberAv3ngers, a group affiliated with Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. APT IRAN has previously claimed attacks against water systems in several US states. The group said earlier attacks in late July targeted water systems in Minnesota, Michigan, Georgia, New Jersey, South Dakota and Arkansas. It then said those attacks were intended to warn about its ability to target critical US infrastructure.AT&T initially said the outage was linked to fiber equipment and cable issues. In an updated statement, the company rejected the hacking group's claim.“We have no evidence to support that claim. Our assessment indicates that attempted cable theft led to the outage. Internet service across Dallas and surrounding areas is operating normally, and we continue to monitor our network and review relevant information,” AT&T said.The company said internet service in Dallas and nearby areas had returned to normal.On August 30, the group claimed it would target more critical infrastructure. According to Threat Beat, APT IRAN said:"We had previously warned that anyone who encroaches on this soil and threatens our beloved Iran will pay for this mistake with their lives," The group also referred to earlier warnings involving Minnesota and said:"You ignored our warnings, and we in Minnesota warned you again. You ignored them again; but this time we will sew the lips and mouths of the American people together."The AT&T outage was first reported Monday, September 7 morning. According to Downdetector data cited by WFAA, customer reports began rising at about 2:18 a.m. A larger increase was recorded from around 10:30 a.m. Reports reached a peak of 5,990 shortly before 3 p.m. The number of reports then dropped quickly, with the outage mostly resolved by around 6 p.m.The outage affected internet, TV and phone services for some customers.
Article Summary: AT&T outage affects internet, TV and phone services for some customers. Iranian- linked hacking group claims responsibility for disruption. APT IRAN has previously claimed attacks against water systems in several US states. AT&T initially said the outage was linked to fiber equipment and cable issues.

Article Title: Hazaribag man drowns while fishing in lake
Article Text:
Hazaribag:





A man drowned in a lake of Hazaribag city while fishing, police said on Monday. The deceased was identified as Mohammad Kalim (50), a resident of Sardar Chowk Mohalla. Officer in-charge of the Lohsighna police station Rohit Kerketta said, “Family members of the deceased told police that he had left home on Sunday morning as usual to catch fish in the lake but did not return till late in the night. They began a search and found his fishing gear and a tiffin box on the bank of the lake. His body was later found floating in the lake. An investigation is under way to ascertain the circumstances leading to the death.”
