Article Title: Gun-toting Brics summit reel puts Delhi constable under departmental inquiry
Article Text:
The video shows the constable drawing a firearm while wearing the summit ID card. (Image Credit: X)





NEW DELHI: A Delhi Police constable wearing a Brics summit 2026 identity card has come under scrutiny after a video showing him making an Instagram reel while handling a firearm went viral on social media.The video has sparked criticism online, with viewers questioning the appropriateness of posting such footage during a high-security international event.The constable is posted in Delhi Police’s northwest district, according to officials. "A departmental inquiry has been initiated against him. He is also likely to be suspended from duties", officials said on Sunday.The development comes as tight security arrangements are in place in the national capital for the second day of the 18th Brics summit 2026 at Bharat Mandapam.Delhi Police on Sunday issued a public advisory warning that traffic movement across the city would be affected due to VVIP movement.The police urged people to use public transport and follow designated alternative routes.Commuters travelling to airports, railway stations and ISBTs were advised to allow extra time for their journeys. Non-destined commercial vehicles have also been barred from entering the city.People travelling to the airport have been advised to use the Metro, which is operating normally without disruptions.
Article Summary: Video shows constable drawing a firearm while wearing the summit ID card. The constable is posted in Delhi Police’s northwest district, according to officials. The development comes as tight security arrangements are in place in the national capital for the second day of the Brics summit 2026.

Article Title: DU official’s post with ABVP’s poll panel triggers row
Article Text:
TOI





New Delhi: Posts by a senior official of Delhi University and a college principal endorsing or appearing alongside the ABVP panel of candidates in the DUSU elections have drawn objections on social media, with some students’ and teachers’ groups questioning the involvement of university authorities in promoting an outfit.A photo posted by DU joint dean of student welfare AK Singh on Facebook with the ABVP panel triggered allegations that he was promoting the group in his official capacity. Singh deleted the post Saturday and issued a clarification on the same platform saying the photograph was taken in the course of his election duty.Singh said Saturday was the last day for withdrawal of nominations and, during the process, he had asked candidates from both ABVP and NSUI to pose for group photographs to share information about the final panels with DU students.“I had requested NSUI’s current DUSU office-bearer Rahul Jhansla several times to come with the NSUI panel for a group photograph. Meanwhile, the ABVP panel had been finalised and I shared its information. However, as the announcement of NSUI candidates was delayed due to an internal dispute, I immediately deleted the ABVP panel post to avoid any allegation of favouritism or discrimination,” Singh clarified.He added that all students were equal, irrespective of their political affiliation or whether they were contesting independently, and that the university’s role was to ensure a “free, fair, impartial and peaceful” election and strict adherence to the Lyngdoh Committee recommendations.DU chief election officer Raj Kishor Sharma said no official complaint had been received. “AK Singh is not a member of the election office. If he has posted anything, it is in his personal capacity, and he is free to do so,” Sharma said.A post by Aditi Mahavidyalaya principal Neelam Rathi as a WhatsApp story has also drawn objections. The post urged students to “Vote, Support, Elect ABVP” and listed its candidates. Rathi toldthat the post was made “by mistake” and was taken down immediately. “In our college, we have not allowed an ABVP candidate to contest because he was not meeting the eligibility criteria. I am not partial to anyone,” she said. Sharma refused to comment on it.RSS-affiliated National Democratic Teachers’ Front member Sunil Sharma posted that Singh had shared election-related information “without making any appeal to anyone to vote”.However, Congress’ student outfit, NSUI, said the post “raises serious questions about the impartiality and neutrality of the university administration”. NSUI media coordinator Ravi Hanuman Pandey said, “We demand immediate removal and dismissal of the official for compromising the sanctity of free and fair student elections.” Congress-affiliated teachers’ group INTEC also demanded Singh’s removal.
Article Summary: A photo posted by DU joint dean of student welfare AK Singh on Facebook with the ABVP panel triggered allegations that he was promoting the group in his official capacity. Singh deleted the post Saturday and issued a clarification on the same platform saying the photograph was taken in the course of his election duty.

Article Title: Minor girl taken to multiple stations over AC fare dispute in Mumbai: Parents
Article Text:
Representational picture





Mumbai: A 17-year-old schoolgirl travelling alone on a suburban train was allegedly taken between several railway stations by railway personnel following a dispute over an AC travel fare and was eventually left at Wadala Road, according to a complaint filed by her parents with Central Railway. The railway, however, said its enquiry found no evidence that the minor was deliberately abandoned.The Class 12 student from Nerul-Seawoods had boarded Train No. 98119 AC Local from Seawoods to Mansarovar on Sept 11. Her parents said she was carrying a valid first-class ticket but was unaware that a separate travel authority was required for AC travel. She was wearing her school uniform, they said.According to the complaint, a ticket examiner stopped the girl and demanded Rs 675. She did not have the money and called her father using a basic mobile phone without internet access. Her father said he was willing to pay any legitimate railway dues and asked to speak directly to the official so that payment could be made through an authorised mechanism.The parents allege that the ticket examiner repeatedly refused to speak to the father or properly identify himself. They later learnt that he was Rajendra Tribhuvan.Concerned about his identity, the father asked his daughter to photograph him.When the train reached Mansarovar, the girl’s mother was travelling to the station to collect her. The parents said they informed the railway personnel that she was on her way and requested that their daughter be allowed to get down. Instead, they allege, she was taken onwards to Panvel.At Panvel, a woman RPF officer became involved. The parents allege that she initially refused to identify herself and spoke to the father harshly. They later identified her as Trushula Dhumal. The parents said they were told the girl would be taken to Belapur, but she was subsequently taken to Wadala Road.The mother followed by another train. The parents allege that the girl was left at Wadala Road without the alleged fine being collected and without being handed over to her mother or another responsible adult.The girl’s father said his daughter had since undergone a counselling session to help her overcome the trauma. “I spoke to her today and understood that the constable handled her like a criminal,” he said, questioning the manner in which a minor carrying a valid First Class ticket was treated.Lata Argade of Upbagariya Pravasi Sangh said the matter required the attention of the Railway Ministry and strict action against the TTE. “The girl was carrying a valid first class ticket and she should have been counselled and let go. I have seen many unauthorised railway personnel taking AC local with valid ticket but TTEs never act against them,” she said.Central Railway said the ticket-checking staff was on authorised duty and that the passenger had been travelling in the AC local without the requisite AC travel authority. The applicable dues were sought through the prescribed HHT QR payment mechanism, but payment could not be completed within the validity period.CR said the matter was brought to the attention of lady RPF staff and supervisory officers at Panvel. After the passenger was identified as a minor, instructions were issued for her safe handover at Wadala Road. According to CR, she was handed over to a railway employee/train manager who represented that he was known to the family, in the presence of RPF and other railway staff.The railway said the staff concerned have been counselled to exercise greater care in similar situations, communicate with parents or guardians wherever practicable and ensure a properly verified handover of minor passengers.The girl’s name has been withheld as she is a minor.
Article Summary: The Class 12 student from Nerul-Seawoods had boarded Train No. 98119 AC Local. Her parents said she was carrying a valid first-class ticket but was unaware that a separate travel authority was required for AC travel. A ticket examiner stopped the girl and demanded Rs 675.

Article Title: ‘Reaction to a fall is not kissing’: Mumbai man gets 1-year jail for forcing himself on mall saleswoman
Article Text:
In a trial that lasted only two months, dismissing the defence, the court found the accused guilty of using criminal force and making unwelcome physical contact with explicit sexual overtures.

Mumbai:





Ruling that a natural reaction to a fall does not involve kissing the victim, a sessions court convicted and sentenced to one year's rigorous imprisonment (RI) a 34-year-old cleaner who claimed he “accidentally slipped and fell” onto a saleswoman at a Borivli (W) mall before forcibly kissing her twice last year.In a trial that lasted only two months, dismissing the defence, the court found Ritesh Armulla guilty of using criminal force and making unwelcome physical contact with explicit sexual overtures.“Even for the sake of argument, if it is considered that a person slipped and fell on another person, the natural reaction would be different from the person kissing the person on whom he fell,” judge said.The offences are covered under BNS sections 74 (assault or the use of criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage, or knowing it is likely to outrage, her modesty) and 75 (sexual harassment) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.Additional Sessions Judge P A Sane said, “The evidence of the victim is convincing and is not disbelievable. There is nothing coming on record as to why the victim will depose against the accused. Moreover, it is coming on record that she did not know the accused before the incident. So there is no possibility that she would falsely involve the accused in this case.” This is one of the few convictions since BNHS replaced IPC.The judge sentenced Armulla to one year’s RI and a fine of Rs 1,000 for the offence under Section 74, and one year’s simple imprisonment with a fine of Rs 500 for the offence under Section 75. Both sentences will run concurrently. The court directed that Rs 1,000 from the fine amount be paid to the victim, whose identity is being withheld, and the remaining amount be credited to the govt.The judge further held, “So this aspect is considered, and there is sufficient reason to believe that the accused intentionally and knowingly did the act; first, by way of kissing the complainant, making her fall down and again kissing her is nothing but an act of outraging the modesty by using criminal force. He followed the complainant to show her to the washroom and, with the intention to outrage her modesty, physically contacted her with explicit sexual overtures. ”The case arose from an incident on Sept 17, 2025, at a mall in Borivli (West). The victim, who was working as a sales girl at the mall, told the court that around 6 pm she was on duty and was walking towards billing counter number 6 after taking a bottle of cold drink. At that time, a man wearing a pink shirt approached and asked her where the washroom was. She pointed towards the direction, but the man repeatedly asked her to show him the washroom.According to the prosecution, after the victim asked the man to go ahead, he went away briefly and returned. The victim deposed that the accused came from behind, knocked against her, asked her to take him to the washroom, and when she refused and proceeded towards the billing counter, he forcibly kissed her, caused her to fall on the ground, and kissed her again. Staff members and people present in the mall caught him. The police were called, and the accused was taken into custody the same day.The court recorded that the victim lodged the FIR immediately on Sept 17, 2025. During investigations, police prepared the spot panchnama, arrested the accused, recorded witness statements, and collected CCTV footage from the mall. The chargesheet was filed on Nov 11, 2025, and charges were framed on July 4, 2026.The prosecution examined four witnesses: the victim, an eyewitness working in the mall, the investigating officer, and a mall employee connected with the CCTV footage. The victim identified Armulla in court and stated that he was the person who had committed the act. The court noted that her testimony was supported by an eyewitness, who said he was present in the mall and saw the accused kiss the victim, make her fall, and kiss her again before being caught.The defence argued that the CCTV footage had not been properly proved, that the prosecution had not examined one mall official named Amar Jadhav, that the hash value of the footage was not produced, and that the accused had not used force or kissed the victim with any intention to outrage her modesty. The defence also suggested that because there was a crowd, the accused may have accidentally dashed against the victim and fallen.The judge accepted that the electronic evidence had weaknesses but held that the oral evidence of the victim and the eyewitness was sufficient and trustworthy. “Even for the sake of argument, it is considered that if a person slipped and fell on another person, the natural reaction would be different from the person kissing the person on whom he fell,” the judge said.Before sentencing, the defence sought leniency, stating that this was the accused’s first offence, that there were no criminal antecedents, and that he had remained in custody since Sept 17, 2025.The court granted set-off for the period already undergone in custody.
Article Summary: Ritesh Armulla found guilty of using criminal force and making unwelcome physical contact with explicit sexual overtures. Court ruled that a natural reaction to a fall does not involve kissing the victim. Armulla sentenced to one year’s RI and a fine of Rs 1,000 for the offence under Section 74.

Article Title: Will start Mumbai march on Sept 15, launch indefinite fast at Azad Maidan on Sept 20: Jarange
Article Text:
Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange announced a five-day march to Mumbai starting Sept 15 on the 15th day of his indefinite hunger strike on Saturday despite appeals from several ministers to defer the programme during Ganeshotsav. Jarange termed the proposed march a “decisive and final” protest, saying he would launch an indefinite fast at Azad Maidan after reaching the state capital on Sept 20.Jarange said he would depart from his native Antarwali Sarati village in Jalna district soon after installing Ganapati idol at 10am on Sept 15. According to the schedule, the march will halt at Patoda (Beed) on Sept 16, Shrigonda in Ahilyanagar on Sept 17, Hadapsar in Pune on Sept 18 and Khopoli in Raigad on Sept 19 before reaching Azad Maidan (Mumbai) on Sept 20. Although Koparkhairane is being considered as an alternative halt, Jarange told his supporters to treat Khopoli as the planned fourth stop.The route from Antarwali Sarati will pass through Shahagad, Gevrai, Beed, Manjarsumba, Limba Ganesh and Patoda before heading towards Mumbai. Jarange said the marchers would cover about 100km a day before reaching each halt.The march is expected to coincide with the Ganesh festival and the run-up to immersion processions, posing a major logistical and security challenge for police and civic authorities.Appealing for peaceful participation, Jarange urged the supporters to maintain discipline. “Nobody should pelt stones or indulge in arson. Vehicles should be driven peacefully,” he said, reiterating that the agitation would remain democratic and non-violent.He also called upon Marathas unable to travel to Mumbai to gather along the route and extend support to the marchers. Jarange urged govt employees, traders, farmers and political workers to join the mobilisation at various points en route.Seeking logistical support, he appealed to financially well-off community members to use their vehicles to ferry protesters towards Mumbai. “Drop us till the outskirts of Mumbai and return. You only have to spend on diesel for four days, but it could transform the lives of Maratha children,” he said.Jarange reiterated that the protesters would travel to Mumbai to secure reservation for the Maratha community and would return only after achieving their objective.Authorities have stepped up security at Antarwali Sarati, deploying additional police personnel with ambulance and fire brigade teams from Saturday.
Article Summary: Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange announced a five-day march to Mumbai starting Sept 15 on the 15th day of his indefinite hunger strike. The march is expected to coincide with the Ganesh festival and the run-up to immersion processions, posing a major logistical and security challenge for police.

Article Title: 2 held for killing pharmacist in Harsul, remanded in five days of police custody
Article Text:
File photo

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Two people were arrested late on Friday nightfor allegedly stabbing a 22-year-old pharmacist to death inside his medical store in Harsul in the afternoon after his family purportedly rejected a marriage proposal for his sister from one of the accused. A court on Saturday remanded the two accused to five days of police custody.Police identified the deceased as Shaikh Mohammed Faisal, who ran the family-owned medical store on Kolthanwadi Road in Karimnagar, Harsul.Harsul police inspector Swati Kedar said Rehan Amin Patel (25) of Karimnagar, one of the two arrested accused, had proposed marriage to Faisal’s 19-year-old sister around five to six months ago. “The proposal was turned down as the family had already arranged her marriage elsewhere. We are investigating the exact sequence of events and the role of the second accused, identified as Sameer Raees Shaikh (24) of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar,” Kedar said.In his complaint, Faisal’s elder brother, Sheikh Mustakim, alleged that the rejection had strained relations between the families and that Patel would often rev his motorcycle outside their house and medical store to harass them.Police said between 12.30pm and 1pm on Friday, Patel and Shaikh allegedly entered Faisal’s medical store and got into an altercation with him.During the argument, Patel allegedly pulled out a knife and stabbed Faisal in the abdomen.The injured pharmacist was rushed to Govt Medical College and Hospital (GMCH) by residents, but doctors declared him dead around 1.25pm.Investigators are probing whether the accused had any prior confrontations with the victim and if others were involved in the attack.
Article Summary: Police identified the deceased as Shaikh Mohammed Faisal, who ran the family- owned medical store on Kolthanwadi Road in Karimnagar, Harsul. A court on Saturday remanded the two accused to five days of police custody.

Article Title: Two arrested, minor detained near Ahilyanagar border for assault on minister’s brother, nephew
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Two men were arrested and a juvenile detained near the Ahilyanagar district border on Friday for allegedly assaulting cabinet minister Atul Save’s elder brother Ajit Save (70) and nephew Ameya Save (35) during a dispute over road work in Paithan taluka a day earlier.The three accused have been booked for attempt to murder and other offences under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, police said.The arrested accused have been identified as 36-year-old Bhalchandra Sattavann and 21-year-old Sangram, alias Karan Pardeshi. Both are residents of Khandewadi village. Also detained was a 17-and-a-half-year-old juvenile. Police said action against the minor would be taken as per legal provisions.According to police, the incident took place on the Babulgaon-Naygavhan road on Thursday afternoon after some youths from Khandewadi allegedly stopped a vehicle over a road-related issue. Ajit Save reached the spot and reportedly told those present that the matter had already been resolved, questioning why vehicles were still being stopped.An argument allegedly followed over work being carried out on both lanes of the road.During the altercation, the accused allegedly pushed Ajit Save into a roadside pit. When Ameya Save intervened and questioned them, Sattavann allegedly attacked him with an iron rod, causing head injuries.Police said Pardeshi and the juvenile then allegedly knocked Ameya to the ground and assaulted him. A person who stepped in to rescue him was also allegedly pushed and manhandled.Based on Ameya Save’s complaint, Bidkin police registered an FIR in the early hours of Friday and launched a search for the suspects.Acting on specific information, a police team tracked the trio down near the Ahilyanagar district border and took them into custody.Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Rural superintendent of pPrakash Jadhav said the investigation was continuing. “The motive behind the attack and the role of all people involved, directly or indirectly, are being probed,” he said.Police said Ameya suffered injuries to his head and left upper arm in the attack.
Article Summary: Two men arrested and a juvenile detained for allegedly assaulting cabinet minister Atul Save’s elder brother Ajit Save (70) and nephew Ameya Save (35) The three accused have been booked for attempt to murder and other offences under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

Article Title: ‘Our Bappa, King of Cleanliness’ contest launched for Ganesh mandals in Sambhajinagar
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





The civic body has launched a cleanliness and environmental awareness competition for public Ganesh mandals, seeking to promote waste segregation, eco-friendly idols and sustainable festival practices during Ganeshotsav.The ‘Amcha Bappa Swachhatecha Raja (Our Bappa, King of Cleanliness)’ contest, organised by the solid waste management department of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Municipal Corporation (CSMC), has entered its second year. Municipal commissioner Amol Yedge said the festival would be used as a platform to promote cleanliness and environmental responsibility.“Several initiatives would be undertaken during the festival to promote cleanliness, environmental conservation and scientific waste management,” Yedge said.Mandals will be evaluated on parameters such as the use of eco-friendly Ganesh idols, DJ-free processions, dustbin facilities and environmentally friendly decorations. Winners will receive first, second and third prizes along with seven consolation awards.“The prizes will include sound systems, CCTV camera sets and LED light sets. The contest is aimed at encouraging mandals to adopt cleaner and environmentally responsible practices during the festival,” said CSMC deputy commissioner Nandakishore Bhombe.Around 250 Ganesh mandals participated in the competition last year, with 10 mandals receiving awards. The civic body has appealed for greater participation this year.As part of a parallel campaign, ‘Ashirwad Bappa, Jagar Swachhatecha’, street plays and band performances highlighting cleanliness, waste segregation and environmental conservation will be held every evening at major mandals across the city.Officials said the initiatives are aimed at ensuring Ganeshotsav serves not only as a religious celebration but also as a platform to spread awareness about cleanliness and scientific waste management.Mayor Sameer Rajurkar urged Ganesh mandals and citizens to participate in large numbers and help carry the message of cleanliness and environmental conservation across the city.
Article Summary: The contest seeks to promote waste segregation, eco-friendly idols and sustainable festival practices during Ganeshotsav. The ‘Amcha Bappa Swachhatecha Raja (Our Bappa, King of Cleanliness)’ contest is organised by Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Municipal Corporation.
